title: A Noetherian local ring of dimension one is regular iff it is a normal domain
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring of Krull dimension $\dim A=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $A$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is generated by one element) if and only if $A$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] (an integral domain integrally closed in its field of fractions).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr, line 29104), equivalence of (3) and (5), with its proof

proof.text: Assume that $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is regular local of dimension one. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], $A$ is a domain. The maximal ideal is generated by one element by the regular-local hypothesis in the statement, and the dimension is one. Thus $A$ has condition (3) of Stacks Lemma 00PD and is a discrete valuation ring by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. A discrete valuation ring is a valuation ring, so [lem-weil-pbc-valuation-ring-normal] gives that $A$ is integrally closed in its fraction field; together with the domain property this is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), proof of (3) implies (5), lines 29124-29148

proof.text: Assume that $A$ is a normal domain of dimension one. The one-dimensional normal-local criterion [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] gives that $A$ is a discrete valuation ring. In the terminology of 00PD, this means in particular that $A$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with maximal ideal generated by one nonzero element. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-principal-maximal-dim-one-regular] yields that $A$ is a regular local ring. The two implications prove the equivalence.
